analysis: This chapter represents the pinnacle of Marianne's arc as she chooses Sense over Sensibility.
Elinor acts as a clinical narrator, guiding the reader through the emotional complexities.
The conflict between economic reality and romantic idealism is sharply drawn.
Willoughby's ruling principle of 'ease' is exposed as his ultimate downfall.
Marianne's hard-won composure is tested by the news of the Dashwood family's future.
The structural irony of the news of Edward's marriage creates a dramatic shift in tone.
The chapter highlights the contrast between Willoughby's selfishness and Marianne's growth.
quotes: I never could have been happy with him
I have been very much to blame in several respects.
Willoughby, in spite of all his many faults, had a heart.
I have now no doubt that he was always more attached to me than to any other woman.
I have nothing to regret—nothing but my own folly.
